title: Is the Judge Its Twin? Post-training makes a model's writing more predictable but barely moves its taste, as a judge, toward predictable writing
abstract: arXiv:2609.32196v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Language models now routinely grade other language models. If post-training makes a model's writing more predictable, it may also teach the same model, as a judge, to reward predictable writing. We test this directly. We follow two open 7-billion-parameter model families, OLMo-2 and Zephyr, from their base models through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and direct preference optimization (DPO), and measure every stage as a writer of short stories and as a judge of story pairs. As writers, the models drift as feared. Each family's trained model finds its stages' stories more familiar in the order base, SFT, DPO, in all ten prompts, and a model from the other family finds the trained stories 7.0 to 9.2 percent (OLMo-2) and 24 to 25 percent (Zephyr) less surprising per token. As judges, they barely move toward predictable writing. Asked which story is better, a question every judge passes a competence check on, no trained judge's preference

translated_title: 评判者是其孪生兄弟吗？后训练使模型的写作更可预测，但作为评判者，其品味几乎不会偏向可预测的写作
translated_abstract: 语言模型如今经常给其他语言模型评分。如果后训练使模型的写作更可预测，它是否也会教导同一个模型（作为评判者）奖励可预测的写作？我们直接测试了这一点。我们跟踪两个开放的70亿参数模型家族——OLMo-2和Zephyr——从它们的基础模型经过监督微调（SFT）和直接偏好优化（DPO）的完整过程，并在每个阶段测量它们作为短篇故事作者和故事对评判者的表现。作为作者，模型如人们担心的那样发生了漂移：每个家族训练后的模型按基础、SFT、DPO的顺序，在全部十个提示中都发现自己各阶段生成的故事更加熟悉，而另一个家族的模型则发现训练后生成的故事每token的惊讶度分别降低了7.0至9.2个百分点（OLMo-2）和24至25个百分点（Zephyr）。但作为评判者，它们几乎不偏向可预测的写作。当被问及哪个故事更好时——一个所有评判者都能通过能力检验的问题——没有任何训练后的评判者的偏好表现出对可预测写作的倾向。
tldr: 该研究发现后训练（SFT和DPO）确实使语言模型的写作变得更加可预测，但这种可预测性偏好并不会迁移到模型作为评判者的角色——训练后的模型在评判故事时几乎不偏向可预测的写作。
en_tdlr: Post-training (SFT and DPO) makes language models' writing more predictable, but this predictability bias does not carry over to their role as judges—trained models show little preference for predictable writing when evaluating stories.
